title: Hof operation event (v2, backup/restore only)
description: One record of the append-only log a running backup or restore operation both streams to stdout (bounded NDJSON) and durably appends to its own operation-journal-v2 (ADR 0006). Scoped strictly to operationKind backup/restore, never apply (see operation-journal-v2.schema.json's own top-level description for why the whole v2 family is scoped this way) - exists only because backup and restore need a genuinely different resumability contract from apply's, not merely because operation-lock-v2/operation-journal-v2 happened to gain an operationKind field: operation-event-v1 (unchanged, still the only event schema apply ever produces) hard-codes apply's own all-or-nothing rule directly into its prose contract - an unresolved `started` blocks resume entirely, and `failed` is always fatal. ADR 0006 promises the opposite for the two new kinds: a backup may crash after `snapshot.create` succeeded for some destinations and not others, and must resume recognizing exactly which; a restore has exactly one privileged checkpoint (`checkpoint.data-restored`) and is otherwise safely restartable from nothing. This schema drops v1's own universal resumability verdict from its prose - which step+attempt is terminal versus resumable is instead decided by the journal's own operationKind-specific reconciliation (a later PR's executor), using this log purely as its evidence. `operationKind` also makes each stdout line self-describing on its own, without a reader cross-referencing the journal first, and lets a consumer confirm an event's own kind actually matches the journal/lock it claims to belong to.

operationKind.description: Which of the two new state machines this event belongs to - never apply. Decides which plan schema `step` below is an id from (backup-plan-v1 for backup, restore-plan-v1 for restore) and which kind-specific reconciliation rules the journal applies to this event.

operationId.description: The whole run this event belongs to - matches the run's own operation-journal-v2 and operation-lock-v2 operationId.

step.description: The bound plan's own operation id this event is about (backup-plan-v1 or restore-plan-v1, per operationKind) - never a free-form message.

attempt.description: 1 for a step's first try; a resumed step that previously failed and is being retried increments this, never reuses attempt 1's own record.

phase.description: started: about to run this step, before any target-side effect. succeeded: the step's own target-side effect completed and was confirmed. failed: the step did not complete - `error` is always present and sanitized. Unlike operation-event-v1, phase alone never determines resumability here - the journal's own operationKind-specific rules do (ADR 0006's own Failure semantics: a backup's `snapshot.create` failing for one destination never blocks retrying the others; a restore's failure before checkpoint.data-restored is safely restartable from nothing, after it never is).

destination.description: Only ever present for a backup-kind event about a per-destination step (snapshot.create, retention.apply) - which configured destination this attempt concerns, so a partial, per-destination failure is identifiable from the event stream alone, without cross-referencing the plan. Absent for every restore event, and absent for a backup event about a step that isn't destination-scoped. Same pattern as backup-plan-v1.schema.json's own $defs/destinationName (services-v1alpha1-compatible), since this always names a real, applied destination.

error.description: Only for phase: failed - a short, sanitized diagnostic. Never a raw exception dump, a secret value, decrypted content, an environment variable's value, or an SSH private-key path.

allOf.description: destination is required for a backup-kind event about a per-destination step (snapshot.create, retention.apply - the step id's own middle segment), and forbidden for every other event - restore, or a backup event about a non-destination-scoped step (maintenance.enter, staging.build, ...). The earlier draft only forbade it outside operationKind: backup, leaving it optional (and so silently droppable) on the very steps it exists for, and unconstrained (so smuggleable) on a backup event about an unrelated step - both real gaps a review round found.
